routes.title: Representations of semisimple Lie algebras, highest weight theory, and the Weyl formulas, Part II: integral and p-adic enveloping algebras
routes.brief: Build the integral and p-adically completed enveloping-algebra theory used by Fu, starting with finite free split sl_2 lattices at odd p and extending only in the stated Ardakov-Wadsley source generality. Import the field PBW, highest-weight, central-character and Casimir theory from LieHighestWeight (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/LieHighestWeight), including the existing Tau Ceti filtration and Casimir declarations; import Mathlib filtered-ring and Ore-localization carriers. Construct integral central reductions, their explicit PBW normal forms, saturated-ideal completion, image lattices in Sym^k, and the separated graded-domain arguments. Prove Fu Lemmas 2.2-2.3, 3.1-3.3 and Proposition 3.4 in declaration-sized parts. The growth endpoint is: a cyclic completed-enveloping module with a generic annihilator has Hom multiplicity in W_k bounded by a multiaffine polynomial of degree at most m-1, uniformly for k in N^m. Include the infinite low-coordinate strips, a nongeneric equal-Casimir counterexample, and the distinction between the integral image lattice and all integral matrices. Construct the affinoid Verma module and central-annihilator theorem in AW14 4.6 with its integral-weight, n>=0 and very-good-prime hypotheses. Distribution algebras and Iwasawa faithfulness belong to NoncommutativeAnalyticDistributions, not this algebraic core. Every definition gets a usable API and at least three tests; no extra characteristic-two theorem is inferred by notation. Reuse the pinned standard integral lattice, enveloping action and Kostant action. Add weighted PBW completions B_rho and bounded central division on the algebraic side; the analytic owner proves their identification with U_r, so this algebraic core has no reverse dependency on analytic distributions. The explicit multiaffine majorant is 2 sum_i alpha_i product_{j!=i}(k_j+1).
routes.reason: The existing highest-weight roadmap owns the ordinary field theory, not these integral completions and uniform central-parameter bounds. This is a Part II, not a re-plan of the upstream roadmap.

routes.title: Locally analytic distributions, growth, and character spaces, Part II: noncommutative distributions and microlocalization
routes.brief: Extend LocallyAnalyticDistributions (LocallyAnalyticDistributions), importing its actual analytic Banach spaces, LF topology and strong duals. Import bounded measures and the completed group ring from p-adic measures, completed group algebras, and characteristic ideals (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L0-L1), profinite foundations from ProfiniteProPGroups, and noetherian/grade inputs from NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa NE.0. Construct odd-prime uniform-group coordinates, Lazard Lie lattices, noncommutative convolution, weighted-c0 radius completions, Frechet-Stein and faithful-flatness theorems of Schneider-Teitelbaum. Construct the source-qualified Ore microlocalization and Lazard comparison with PadicEnvelopingAlgebras. Prove finite-dimensional/isotypic quotient recovery, the finite crossed-product radius description, central strong duality and cofinal-limit comparison, and the separated topological PBW theorem needed in Fu section 5. The endpoint is injectivity Q_p[[G]] -> Uhat_lambda for the product of m first-congruence SL_2(Z_p) groups and every lambda in Z_p^m. Keep the direct analytically induced-character proof and the all-integral AW14 Verma route distinct; the latter requires finite coefficient extension and faithful descent. Do not identify bounded coefficients with a norm completion, or use the unramified Ore set over a ramified DVR. Include Banach-Iwasawa duality and algebraic matrix-coefficient comparisons without duplicating field highest-weight theory. Require naturality, handedness, norm and quotient APIs and tests on the trivial representation, a ramified coefficient ring, and an integral parameter not induced over Q_p. This does not build Colmez or the geometric locally analytic-vectors theorem. Import the weighted PBW completion and bounded-division theorem, then identify U_(r_n) with B_(p^n). Prove the finite crossed-product Ext comparison before grade invariance. Record that large nonintegral central parameters can give the zero ring, and do not export Fu5.7 as a nonzero-domain theorem without a parameter qualification.
routes.reason: The existing locally analytic roadmap has function spaces and abelian transforms but no general noncommutative radius/crossed-product/microlocal theory. The same new foundation is reusable beyond Fu and must not be hidden in a Bianchi-only proof.

routes.title: Arithmetic locally symmetric spaces and their cohomology, Part II: weight-aspect multiplicity bounds
routes.brief: Build on Arithmetic locally symmetric spaces and their cohomology (ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces) and Completed cohomology, homology and arithmetic towers - Part II (CompletedCohomologyPartII). Import their actual quotients, algebraic local systems, finite chain models, completed homology, torsion theorem in the no-discrete-series case, and finite-level descent spectral sequence. Import NoncommutativeAnalyticDistributions and PadicEnvelopingAlgebras rather than reconstruct their rings. First prove Fu Theorem 1.4: for any finitely generated Q_p[[G]]-module M of rank a, G a product of m first-congruence SL_2 groups at odd p, the difference between dim H_0(G,M tensor W_k) and a product_i(k_i+1), and every positive-degree homology dimension, are bounded by one multiaffine polynomial of degree <=m-1, for all k in N^m. Split the upper and lower rank estimates before dimension shifting. Then for fixed level over a number field F with r_2>0 prove dim S_kappa <= C Delta(kappa)/min_v kappa_v, with even entries >=2, Delta=product_real kappa times product_complex kappa^2, and parallel bound O(kappa^([F:Q]-1)). Prove the Bianchi O(kappa) specialization; derive two-sided linear growth only with the FGT base-change lower-bound level hypotheses. Distinguish cuspidal, interior, ordinary and compact-support cohomology and prove the bounded-boundary bridge for the latter interpretation in degrees one and two. Include change of level, finite coefficient-field comparison, nontrivial versus trivial coefficients, and boundary normalization. No epsilon loss, leading constant, arbitrary-level lower bound or totally-real saving is asserted without a separate theorem.
